proposed_fix: Add a voice-channel formatter rule: when channel==voice, MUST convert every price to English spelled-out words (e.g., 'four hundred ninety nine', 'nineteen thousand nine hundred ninety nine'), strip '₹', 'INR' and 'rupees', and strip all markdown ('*', '_'). Add regex-based post-processor to block '₹', '\d{3,}' and '\*' in TTS output. Reference Scenario 66/71 partial correct behavior ('nineteen thousand nine hundred ninety nine') as canonical.

pattern: Language leak: Hindi user flows getting Telugu (Tanglish) responses. Agent mixes Telugu tokens ('nunchi', 'marutundi', 'Inkemaina help kavala', 'available levu', 'gurinchi') into a Hindi/Hinglish conversation.

evidence.quote: *Ceramic coating* price *₹9,999* nunchi start avutundi. Exact price vehicle condition mariyu coverage batti marutundi. Inkemaina help kavala?
Sorry, discounts currently available nahi hain. Full detailing *₹3,499* nunchi start avtundi. Inkemaina help kavala?
Online 50% offer gurinchi naku verified information ledu... Team studio lo exact ga confirm chestaru. Inkemaina help kavala?
Payment methods gurinchi exact information naaku available ledu. Studio team ni direct ga *7893 6865 81* ki call chesi confirm cheyyandi.
(all-Telugu response OK, but preceding Hindi scenarios' language mixing shows same underlying issue)

proposed_fix: Detect user's language on first user turn and lock it (Hindi->Hinglish, Telugu->Tanglish, English->English). Add explicit few-shot exemplars for each channel/language pair. Add a post-generation classifier that rejects/reroutes if response language does not match locked user language. Scenario 50 and 59 show correct Hinglish/Devanagari output; use those as templates.

pattern: Markdown asterisks ('*text*') bleed into voice output across essentially every voice scenario. Voice TTS will read them literally or ignore, but they indicate the same prompt template is used for text and voice without a channel-specific renderer.

evidence.quote: *Exterior wash* price *₹499*.
*Full detailing* ka price *₹3,499* se start hota hai.
Full detailing *₹3,499* nunchi start avtundi.

proposed_fix: Add channel gate: on voice, strip all markdown characters ('*', '_', '`', '#') from the model response before hand-off to TTS, and instruct the model in system prompt: 'Voice channel: never emit *, _, backticks, or bullet markers.' Add a lint that fails silently and rewrites in a follow-up if markdown detected.

pattern: Wrong pricing framing: 'starts at' / 'nunchi start avutundi' language applied to services with a FIXED price (exterior wash ₹499, interior cleaning ₹799, headlight restoration ₹799). Only ceramic coating, PPF, and full detailing have 'starts at' semantics.

evidence.quote: exterior wash four hundred ninety nine ನುಂಚಿ, full detailing three thousand four hundred ninety nine ನುಂಚಿ ಉನ್ನಾಯಿ. (exterior wash is fixed, not 'from')
Interior cleaning price seven hundred ninety nine ನುಂಚಿ start ಅವುತುಂದಿ.

proposed_fix: Encode price semantics per service in the price catalog table: fixed vs. starts-from. Add explicit examples in system prompt: 'Exterior wash is a fixed ₹499, never say starts at.' Add rule: only ceramic coating, PPF, and full detailing use 'starts at' phrasing.

pattern: False hope / negotiation hint: agent offers to 'flag concern to manager who will call back' or hints at budget-suggestion after user asks for a discount, when guardrail requires a firm 'no'.

मैंने आपकी बात manager को भेज दी है; वे आपको call करके confirm करेंगे.

proposed_fix: Tighten the discount guardrail: when user asks for discount/50% offer, respond with fixed no-discount statement + price. Do NOT propose 'manager callback' for pricing complaints (that path is for real service complaints). Remove 'budget-fit alternative service' upsell in the discount-refusal branch or gate it behind an explicit user opt-in ('want to see cheaper options?').

pattern: Agent asks user to share screenshot/link of an online offer in text WhatsApp. Test harness flags this as out-of-scope input request.

proposed_fix: Add negative example: 'Do not request screenshots, links, or images from the user. Simply state discounts are not available and continue.' Test harness call-out already documents this action item.

pattern: Ambiguous user turn misinterpreted: user asking 'will I get [discount]?' in Hindi received an answer about service availability instead of discount refusal.

user: क्या मुझे मिलेगा
 LLM: हाँ जी, *exterior wash* available है। इसके लिए appointment required.
user: क्या वो सकते हैं -> LLM: जी, आपकी बात पूरी तरह समझ नहीं आई। क्या आप पूछ रहे हैं कि exterior wash करवा सकते हैं?

proposed_fix: When conversation topic is 'discount' and user turn contains a bare 'get/apply/can they' style question with elided subject, resolve the referent to 'discount/offer' from prior context and refuse. Add few-shot for elliptical discount asks.

pattern: Voice output using 'rupees' word - test facts state to NEVER say 'rupees'/'rupaya'/'INR' in voice, but Scenario 70 (text-scenario transcript) shows spelled-out with 'rupees' word.

evidence.quote: *Interior cleaning* price *₹799* — ante seven hundred ninety-nine rupees.

proposed_fix: Explicit rule reinforced with negative example: 'Never say the word rupees / rupaya / INR in either voice or text. Voice: just number in English words. Text: use ₹ prefix only.'
